title: Listening to Your Favorite Music May Help Ease Pain
paragraphs: Bob Marley once sang, "One good thing about music, when it hits you, you feel no pain." And he may have been onto something — as long as it's the right kind of music.
A group of researchers in Zürich, Switzerland, have found that listening to your favorite music could help relieve pain during small medical procedures.

They looked at 204 adults having an MRI scan. Before the scan, each patient needed a cannula — a small tube placed into a vein to deliver a liquid that makes the MRI images clearer. The pain is usually brief, but can feel strong for some.

The patients were divided into four groups. One listened to relaxation music similar to what you might hear at a spa. Another listened to Mozart's Sonata KV 448 — a lively piece that several studies have linked to therapeutic benefits. The third group chose their own favorite songs, while the fourth listened to no music at all.
The researchers asked the patients to rate their pain before the cannula went in, right after it went in, then again 30 seconds later, and after two minutes.
​​Listening to one's favorite music had the strongest effect, with patients reporting less pain both after 30 seconds and after two minutes.
Mozart helped too, but only among those already in pain before the procedure — and the researchers aren't sure why.
Relaxation music and no music had no effect on pain, however.

The researchers say relaxation music may be easy to tune out because of its slow speed and lack of dynamics, while people's favorite music may be more distracting because it's familiar and easy to follow.

​​Exactly how music reduces pain remains unclear, but the researchers say it may help distract the brain, lower stress and cause the release of endorphins — the body's natural pain-relieving chemicals.
They hope future studies will show whether music can help with stronger or longer-lasting pain as well.
